```text
VPIP/PFR
Definition: VPIP/PFR show the % of the time a player voluntarily puts money
into the pot and raises pre-floprespectively. This ratio is key to typing players
from an early stare and getting a feel for how wide their ranpes are. They'rethe
most essential HUD statsthere are.
Reliability (No. of Hands)
10 - Poor: Certainly not useless. A 60/D player over 10 hands is very likely to be
a Fish where as a 25/25 is very likelyto be a Rag.
50 = Okay: Gives a very reliable rough idea of player type but not much more.
100 = Decent: By now the statsare converging to something on avorage fairly
close to the truth. It's still nermal to have stats out by 5-10% or so due to
variance of being dealt less or more good hands than normal.
200 = Good: Reliabilityis now going to be within a few % more often than not.
500 = Excellent: A much more accurate picture.
Interpretation (Big Gap)
Players with large disparity such as 45/11or 36/4 are always weaker players and
of the passive sort. They call more than they raise.
20/4 =Tight Passive Fish: This ployer is timid and likes to play a tight range
meekly.
40/12 = Loase Passive Fish: This player limps a lot, calls a lot and doesn't usually
get aggressive without what they considera good hand.
70/14 = Passive Whale: This player plays far coo many hands and rarely raises.
Interpretation (Small Gap)
Players with stats like 24/18 and 18/16 are more likely to be Regulars as these
statsbecome too high they go back into the realms of Fish.
16/11 = Nit:This player folds far too much and bets and raises mainly for value.
19/16 - Tight Reg: This player folds too much but by a lesser margin. He is more
competentthan the nit.
23/19 = Standard Reg: Solid stats, this player is on averoge strongerthan the
previoustwo.
27/22 = Loose Reg: This player is usually aggressive but not always good.
41/36= Aggro Fish: This player raises too many hands and has poorly controlled
often ill timed aggression
76/52= Aggro Whale: Thisplayer isjust tossing money around, be patient and
take it.
```

```text
many hands that would be negative EV
opens at tighter tables are now
profitable due to the high frequency with
which he gets to play a pot heads-up
(just two players involved) with the
Fish, in position. So Hero adds some
extra hands with both good pair potential
```
